slot.brief: Graham's law: compare rates or times of effusion of two gases; give ratio of molecular masses and solve for unknown gas identity or time ratio.

stem: For equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure, methane effuses in $20$ s and gas X in $30$ s. Find the molar mass of X. Take $M(\text{CH}_4)=16\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For equal volumes, effusion time is proportional to √M. Thus M_X = 16(30/20)² = 36 g mol⁻¹.

working:
$\dfrac{t_X}{t_{\text{CH}_4}}=\dfrac{r_{\text{CH}_4}}{r_X}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M_X}{M_{\text{CH}_4}}}$
$\dfrac{30}{20}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M_X}{16}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad M_X=36\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Independent check: For equal volumes, effusion time is proportional to √M. Thus M_X = 16(30/20)² = 36 g mol⁻¹.
solution:
For equal volumes, the effusion time is proportional to the square root of molar mass:
$$\frac{t_X}{t_{\mathrm{CH}_4}}=\sqrt{\frac{M_X}{M_{\mathrm{CH}_4}}}$$
$$M_X=16\left(\frac{30}{20}\right)^2=36\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$$
